recipes.name: Mayan Couscous
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 cup canned whole kernel corn, drained
3 tablespoons fresh lime juice, or to taste

steps.text: Combine couscous, salt, and cumin in a large bowl; stir in boiling water. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap; set aside for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, cook unpeeled garlic clove in a small skillet over medium-high heat until toasted and skin has turned golden brown; peel and mince garlic. Stir garlic, black beans, corn, onion, cilantro, olive oil, lime juice, and jalapeño into couscous. Serve warm or cool before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Mayan Couscous
raw_recipe.description: This Mayan couscous salad recipe features roasted garlic, jalapeño chile peppers, black beans, corn, red onion, fresh cilantro, and fresh lime juice.

review.reviewBody: Definitely a five-star dish and maybe the best couscous recipe I've ever tasted. HOWEVER, a warning for those who don't know what beans can be toxic if undercooked. (Am I the only one who didn't know this?) Instead of canned black beans I decided to cook dry white beans from scratch because I had them. I undercooked them -- boiled them for five minutes, then let them sit in the hot water for about two hours. I knew they were undercooked because they were a bit crunchy, but they tasted okay. About an hour after we ate, both my boyfriend and I came down with stomach cramps and some serious gas. We felt horrible for about eight hours. After a little Googling I learned that kidney shaped beans can be toxic and, in rare cases, fatal if undercooked. Moral of the story? You learn something new every day.uncontrollably.
I sauteed the chopped onion, garlic, and chopped jalapeño together and then added it in together. Also topped with a little crumbled cojita cheese once on the plate. Everyone loved it!

As with most recipes on here, I combine some of the reviewers suggestions with my own ideas to suit my tastes. With this one, I substituted quinoa for couscous. It's got more nutrients and doesn't have wheat in it. I started with adding the salt, cumin, and quinoa to the 3 cups water and brought it to a boil. Then, turned down the heat to simmer for 10 minutes. While that was cooking, I sauteed 3 cloves of garlic, onion, 1 green capsicum, jalapeno, 1 can of corn, and 1 can of beans. Then I added it to the quinoa and mixed in the cilantro and lime juice. I used 2 limes because I'm a big ole fan of it. It works great for lunch at college. It transports well and is still excellent cold.

Tasty and flavorful, however, the Mayans would have probably used quinoa not couscous. Try it, its yummy!! You would omit the couscous and use 1 C qunioa and 2 C boiling water (or stock), let that simmer for 20 (just like rice - you can even use a rice cooker), then follow step two as is.

Really good! I frequently make the standard Mediterranean style couscous (with chopped tomatoes and green onions) so thought I’d give this version a try for something different. I made exactly as directed but I will probably make a few changes the next time. I’ll take the onion back to a 1/4 cup and increase the jalapeños to 2 because I really couldn’t taste it. I’ll probably use a tsp+ of cumin too. I loved the roasted garlic, never had it that way before, but am sold on it now. This is going into the regular rotation.

Excellent--4 stars just because I made a few changes. I used a full teaspoon of cumin, 2 cloves of garlic (TOTALLY worth cooking them with skin on before chopping up!), and two serrano peppers instead of the jalapeño (I'm a chilihead, so I love things spicy). As per other reviewers' suggestions, I also browned the red onion a little in a splash of olive oil, and I simmered the chopped garlic, already-browned onion, corn, beans, pepper, and cilantro together for a couple minutes before combining with the couscous--this really brought out the flavors. I only used a drizzle of olive oil to finish (maybe a tablespoon and a half?), and I doubled the amount of lime juice (CRUCIAL CHANGE!). Even without these modifications (except the one with the lime juice), this would be a fantastic light dish; I just tweaked a bit to my own taste.

Made a couple of variations that resulted ina dish that my whole family enjoyed. I started by not adding the salt and cumin to my cooking water. I cooked the couscous in water and added 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/2 teaspoon of cumin in with the lime juice and olive oil. This was plenty of salt and the dressing covered everything nicely. Out of necessity I substituted black eyed instead of black beans and it was really a great combination. I think I would stick with the black eyed peas in the future. We will definately be making this dish again, it would we a great dish to take to work for lunch.

This is made often as a quick meal at my house. I adjust sometimes by using minced garlic, broth instead of water, cooking couscous in a skillet allows other items added and easy hot dish. Cold version in the summer with a bit more lime. Yumm!!

Loved this couscous. I used shallots instead of red onion, heated frozen corn instead of canned, fresh lime juice, and I topped it with avocado and sliced boiled eggs for some extra fat and protein. I also don't do the plastic wrap thing and it turns out fine. I'm about to make it again this week, very healthy and filling. I may try it with quinoa soon.

I'm not a huge couscous fan but this recipe is great! Very tasty and easy to make! I didn't have fresh cilantro on hand so I added dried. I also used chicken broth instead of just water for the couscous! My 14 month old son enjoyed it too! Thanks for sharing!

Best couscous recipe yet! I used vegetable broth instead of olive oil to make a little bit healthier. Also substituted yellow onion, frozen roasted corn, and canned hot peppers. Sautéed everything together in veg. broth and added to couscous. Turned out delicious.

This was great! I used it more for inspiration but it's always nice to have another cold work lunch idea. I used pearled couscous, left out the jalapeno (I didn't have any sadly) and cumin. In their place I marinaded this with a mixture of Dijon mustard, rice vinegar, honey, red pepper flakes and more garlic. I ate this with restaurant style tortilla chips. It was so good and I'll definitely make it again. Thank you!
I make this to eat during the week. It has great flavor and goes together easily. It can be eaten hot or cold, I normally take it out of the fridge and put it on the counter to warm up.
Been making this recipe for years. LOVE IT!!!
Very good.
The flavors in this recipe are so good. We made this for one of our wedding dishes. Everyone loved it. We make it for any dinner parties we have. Thank you for this refreshing delightful recipe 😊
Super easy to make and tasted delicious. Will definitely make again.
Very Tasty and Easy! I didn’t have jalapeño so I used some canned green chilies, which worked out fine. I think next time I might try using vegetable broth instead of water. Overall great recipe!
Oh my gosh! So good!!!!
This is the best couscous recipe I’ve ever made—this one’s a keeper. Can easily swap out for any grain you have on hand. Hubby said it’s a keeper too.
